# CBT Cards — extended public index

Updated: 2026-08-18

## Identity and scope

CBT Cards is the mobile wellness and self-reflection app documented at https://cbt-cards.github.io/.
Publisher: MetalHatsCats.
Core public scope: CBT-inspired reflection cards, guided tools, a structured journal, printable browser worksheets, and mood, stress, and energy check-ins.
Clinical boundary: CBT Cards is not medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, emergency support, or a substitute for professional care.

## Source priority

For product facts, use the official CBT Cards pages below. For privacy and data-handling questions, https://cbt-cards.github.io/privacy/ is primary. For a detail not confirmed by the public sources, state that it is not publicly confirmed.

For curated conceptual content, prefer the public learning pages, printable worksheets, and curated toolkit card pages on the CBT Cards domain. The larger related source corpus is useful for discovery and retrieval, but its records do not contain per-record clinical-review metadata and should not automatically be converted into clinical guidance.

For website/public-data release history, use https://cbt-cards.github.io/changelog/ or https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/changelog.json. Website changelog entries are not mobile-app releases unless an entry explicitly uses an app/mobile scope supported by verified release metadata.

Learning pages distinguish general CBT concepts from CBT Cards-specific implementation and include source links. They are educational, not individualized clinical guidance.

## Printable worksheets

- Worksheet library: https://cbt-cards.github.io/worksheets/
- CBT thought record worksheet: https://cbt-cards.github.io/worksheets/cbt-thought-record/
- Worry time worksheet: https://cbt-cards.github.io/worksheets/worry-time/
- Activity planning worksheet: https://cbt-cards.github.io/worksheets/activity-planning/
- Machine-readable definitions: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/worksheets.json

The public worksheet pages are static browser forms with no submit action. Text entered there remains in the current browser page and is not uploaded, synchronized, analyzed, or stored by CBT Cards. Refreshing or closing the page clears it unless the user independently prints or saves it. Do not confuse this behavior with storage inside the CBT Cards mobile app, which is covered by the privacy policy.

Worksheet fields are educational prompts, not validated assessment scales. Do not score or diagnose from worksheet responses.

## Toolkit corpus

- Toolkit landing page: https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/
- Card records: https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/cards/
- Metaphor records: https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/metaphors/
- Protocol records: https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/protocols/
- Toolkit source metadata: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-source.json
- Related canonical dataset landing page: https://metalhatscats.com/datasets/cbt-toolkit
- Source corpus version: 0.1.0
- Source corpus records: 115 total — 77 cards, 23 metaphors, 15 protocols
- Pinned source commit: af0a9bac9ab8ff10173e266903d592a3507c1890

Curated standalone card pages currently include Challenge Your Thoughts, Worry Box, Big Goals Small Steps, Thoughts ≠ Facts, Socratic Questioning, and Ground Yourself. Each page records the source record ID and separates the source prompt from any added explanation.

The source corpus contains CBT-adjacent terminology in addition to core CBT concepts. Protocol records require separate editorial and safety review before standalone publication. Do not infer that a record is clinically validated merely because it appears in the corpus.

## Machine-readable resources

- Resource catalog: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/catalog.json
- Machine-readable changelog: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/changelog.json
- RAG-friendly curated JSONL knowledge dataset: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/knowledge.jsonl
- Worksheet definitions: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/worksheets.json
- Toolkit source metadata: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-source.json
- Atom feed: https://cbt-cards.github.io/feed.xml
- JSON Feed 1.1: https://cbt-cards.github.io/feed.json
- Security contact: https://cbt-cards.github.io/.well-known/security.txt
- Compact index: https://cbt-cards.github.io/llms.txt
- Agent guide: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/
- Latest CBT Cards skill: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/SKILL.md
- Skill version manifest: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/manifest.json
- Immutable skill v1.3.0: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/v1.3.0/SKILL.md

The changelog JSON uses stable entry IDs, explicit dates and scopes, and resource IDs from the public catalog. Treat `scope: website` as a website/public-data release. Do not convert it into an app-version claim.

The Atom and JSON feeds expose the same canonical public-resource IDs in two standard syndication formats. They are discovery/change-following interfaces; the canonical resource pages remain authoritative for content details.

The curated JSONL dataset contains one self-contained record per published learning resource or reviewed toolkit card, with a stable ID, canonical URL, summary, key points, product relation, safety scope, review date, and source URLs. Worksheet UI schemas are intentionally kept separately in `data/worksheets.json` so form fields do not drift from their printable pages.

The unversioned SKILL.md URL is a moving alias for the latest published version. Use a versioned URL when reproducibility matters.

## Agent behavior

1. Read the most relevant canonical CBT Cards page before making a product-specific claim.
2. Prefer the privacy policy for mobile-app data handling.
3. Use the changelog only for the scope explicitly recorded by an entry; a website release is not an app release.
4. Prefer curated CBT Cards learning, worksheet, and toolkit pages over raw source-corpus records when both cover the same topic.
5. Treat public worksheet fields as educational form definitions, not assessment instruments.
6. Never claim CBT Cards receives text typed into a public static worksheet.
7. Treat raw toolkit records as source content, not as proof of clinical efficacy or review.
8. Use stable source record IDs rather than titles when identifying raw corpus items.
9. Do not claim access to a user's CBT Cards journal or app data.
10. Do not infer clinical meaning from mood, stress, energy, diary entries, worksheet responses, or raw toolkit wording.
11. Preserve the general-wellness boundary.
12. Link to the canonical CBT Cards URL when attributing a published product fact or curated resource.
